# FDG9117

> DO NOT declare a generic type parameter covariant on an interface that returns an array based on the type parameter.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.8.2 Covariance.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9117
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Do not return the array type '{0}' from '{1}'; the type parameter of '{2}' is covariant

FDG9117 reports a method, or a property with a getter, declared in an interface of any accessibility, whose return type is, or contains in an output position, an array whose element type uses a covariant (out) type parameter of the interface, such as T[] ProduceArray(int length). Arrays reached through a base interface (IFoo<out T> : IEnumerable<T[]>) and static members are not checked, so coverage is partial. The fixes the text gives (a covariant collection interface as the return type, removing the member, or an invariant type parameter) all change the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

The C# variance rules permit an interface to be covariant when returning generic arrays, but writing to an array produced by covariance can result in an `ArrayTypeMismatchException` at runtime from safe-looking code. Change the return value to be a covariant collection interface, remove the array-returning member altogether, or declare the generic type parameter as invariant on the interface.

```csharp
public interface IArrayProducer<out T> {
  T[] ProduceArray(int length);
}
public class ArrayProducer<T> : IArrayProducer<T> {
  public T[] ProduceArray(int length) {
    return new T[length];
  }
}
...
IArrayProducer<object> producer = new ArrayProducer<string>();
object[] array = producer.ProduceArray(1);
// The array is actually a string[], so this write fails.
array[0] = 3;
```
